The 'd' is sometimes silent in English.

The 'd' may be alone, or it may be in a 'dg' combination.

Read these words out loud. Concentrate on the pronunciation of them - notice the silent ‘d'.

Stress in Phrasal Verbs and Breaking Sentences Into Parts
When you say a long sentence in English, you break it into distinct parts, each with its own intonation. You use the rise and fall of your voice to show the listener when you are or are not finished.

You break long sentences into parts, called clauses. Each clause has its own subject and verb (and sometimes object).

You also pause or break when you see a comma. A comma can separate a word or phrase from the rest of the sentence, or show where a clause ends.

For example:
When I checked into a hotel, // I would pick up a map and talk over my ideas with the concierge// who was more than happy to help.

At the end of each clause, you use rising intonation to show the listener that the sentence is not finished.

When you give opinions, the lead in to the opinion or reply is separated with a comma.

You also use stress when saying phrasal verbs.
If the phrasal verb is not separable, then you stress the verb.

Example: go over
Let's go over the menu. (go over - is not finished without the object menu.)
I didn't hear back.

images.text:
Sally,

I haven't heard from you about going shopping for spices on Wednesday. I'm not going to let you dodge this outing! You pledged to help and I can't get on without you shopping with me in Boston! Can I come by or call and set up our day out? You have to come along!

I want to catch up and talk about everything you've been doing! We can stop in at some nice sandwich shop for lunch. I need to come up with some more ideas for the event night. I thought I'd get some Spicy Rice Night badges made while I was in Boston. The chef told me to go for it! I also think the night calls for brightly colored handkerchiefs, or rather napkins, for the tables. We're having cheese wedges melted into a spicy rice dish as a starter.

I thought the patrons would go in for some handsome dancers for entertainment. I've had to see to all of the arrangements by myself for this thing. It's tiring, to say the least!

I know I'm difficult to put up with sometimes when I'm on edge, but I do so miss your company! You can still get away with taking the day off right? I really need a dose of your positive outlook as the big day looms!

V
